observation.visible_scene: A close-up, dimly lit shot of a person playing a classical (nylon-string) guitar. The guitar's wooden top, decorative rosette, and round sound hole sit at left-center; the fretboard runs diagonally toward the right and is mostly out of focus. The player's right hand hovers over the strings near the sound hole, while the left hand's fretting fingers appear as a blurred shape in the foreground over the neck. The player's light-colored shirt and tan trouser leg are partially visible at the frame edges against a plain wall.
visible_changes: The right hand performs a continuous plucking cycle: the index finger repeatedly extends toward the strings, contacts them, and then retracts/curls back, while the thumb rests near the lower strings.
The left (fretting) hand shifts its finger placement on the neck, with fingers pressing down and lifting in sequence, changing the fretted note over time.
The guitar and hands remain in roughly the same overall position across the excerpt; only the fingers move, with at most a slight handheld wobble of the framing.
The motion is already ongoing at the first frame and continues through the last frame without a clear start or stop.
outside_clip_unknowns: The music being played and any audio are not observable.
The full posture of the player, the headstock, and the bridge are outside the cropped view.
Whether this is the beginning or end of a piece is unknown; the segment is an arbitrary slice of continuous playing.
uncertain_details: Exact fret positions and string numbers are indeterminate because the fretboard and left hand are heavily out of focus.
It is unclear whether small shifts in framing come from camera movement or from the player's body swaying.
